question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6.75% per annum rate of interest deposited on 25 February 2024 and withdrawn on 26 April 2024.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total days between 25 Feb and 26 Apr 2024 = 4 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 26 (Apr) = 61 days.

Since 2024 is a leap year, time in years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year.

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

SI = (4000 × 6.75 × 1) ÷ (100 × 6) = 270 ÷ 6 = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 6.75% per annum

Date of deposit = 25 February 2024

Date of withdrawal = 26 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 
 25 Feb 2024
 P = ₹4000
 
 26 Apr 2024
 SI = ?
 
 T = 61 days
 R = 6.75% p.a.
 
 
 SI = ₹45

**Calculations:**

⇒ Year 2024 is a leap year (divisible by 4), so February has 29 days.

⇒ Number of days in February (excluding deposit date) = 29 − 25 = 4 days

⇒ Number of days in March = 31 days

⇒ Number of days in April (including withdrawal date) = 26 days

⇒ Total time (T) in days = 4 + 31 + 26 = 61 days

⇒ Total days in leap year = 366

⇒ Time in years (T) = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6.75 × 1/6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (40 × 6.75) ÷ 6

⇒ SI = 270 ÷ 6

⇒ SI = 45

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leap Year Calculation

A year is a leap year if it is perfectly divisible by 4. Century years must be divisible by 400. In leap years, February has 29 days and the total number of days in the year is 366.

Counting Days for Interest

When calculating interest between two dates, typically the day of deposit is excluded but the day of withdrawal is included. This ensures the exact number of days is counted accurately.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated uniformly on the initial principal amount throughout the period, whereas Compound Interest calculates interest on both the principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.
